summary: A. B. Gajendragadkar was an Indologist who served as Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and as Lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College, Dharwad.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, Muller earned his PhD from Stony Brook University (1988) and studied at the University of Virginia. He held professorships at Toyo Gakuen University (~1997–2008) and the University of Tokyo (~2008–2019).

A. H. Armstrong was a philosopher who studied at Jesus College (~1928–1932). He held academic posts at Swansea University (~1936–1939), the University of Malta (~1939–1946), Cardiff University (~1946–1950), and the University of Liverpool (~1950–1972).

A scholar of linguistics and Indology, Ramanujan studied at the University of Mysore, Maharaja's College, and Indiana University. He taught at Baroda College (~1957–1958), the University of Chicago (~1962–1993), and Harvard University (~1983–1984).
A. N. Krishna Aiyangar was an Indologist who served as Joint Editor for Brahmavidyā: The Adyar Library Bulletin (attested 1940–1942) at the Adyar Library and Research Centre.
A. N. Narasimhia worked in linguistics and Indology, completing doctoral research under Ralph Lilley Turner (attested 1941). He held a post at the University of Mysore.

An Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar, Jackson studied at Columbia University and Halle-Wittenberg under Edward Washburn Hopkins. He taught at Columbia (~1886–1891; ~1895–1935) and served as Corresponding Secretary of the American Oriental Society (1908).
A. W. Barber is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1984). He held a post at the University of Calgary (attested 1998).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology, Proffitt completed his MA at CU Boulder and PhD at the University of Michigan under Micah L. Auerback. In ~2015, he became assistant professor of Japanese Studies at University at Albany, SUNY.

Abdur Rehman is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Peshawar (attested 1988).

Abel Bergaigne was a French scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Michel Bréal (~1867–1869). He served as répétiteur at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1888) and held a post at the University of Paris (~1885–1888).

Abigail I. MacBain is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at McMaster University (attested 2008), where she studied under Mark Rowe, James A. Benn, and Shayne Clarke.
Abraham Zablocki is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his PhD from Cornell University. He held an academic post at Agnes Scott College (attested 2008).

Achim Bayer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his MA under David P. Jackson and PhD (-2005) under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg. He was a research associate at LMU Munich (2004–2006).

Adalbert Bezzenberger was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Göttingen and LMU Munich, including under Theodor Benfey. He held a post at the University of Göttingen (~1874–1880) and founded Beiträge zur Kunde der indogermanischen Sprachen.

Adalbert Kuhn was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1833–1837). He served as Direktor of Köllnisches Gymnasium (~1870–1881) and founded Zeitschrift für vergleichende Sprachforschung.

Adam Bowles is an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed his doctorate under Greg Bailey (attested 2004). He served as senior lecturer in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland (attested 2016–2018).
Adam Hardy is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at The Royal Grammar School, High Wycombe, he held a post at Cardiff University (~2000).

Adam Pearcey is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier, alongside training under various traditional Buddhist teachers.

Adeu Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under traditional teachers including Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima, Samten Gyatso, and Chögon Rinpoche, and taught Tsoknyi Rinpoche.
